full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff appellant instituted the aforesaid title suit for declaration of his title and for khas possession by ejecting the defendant-respondent. His case is that the suit land measuring 8 81 acres of R.S. plot No.2956 appertaining to R.S. Khatian No.776. jote No.86 at rental of Tk. 34/- belonged to Sarada Kripa Lala. The land was settled with Sarada Kripa Lala in 1931. On 4th January 1939 he made a will of the suit land and other lands in favour of his daughter in-law Madhabi Lata who obtained probate of the will from the District Judge, Chittagong in Civil Suit No.4 of 1939. Since then she had been in actual physical possession of the land on payment of rent. Sarada Kripa Lala had mortgaged some properties other than the suit lands to Mohaluxmi Bank Ltd. which obtained a decree against him in a mortgage suit. The Bank purchased the entire mortgage properties in execution of the mortgage decree on 14th March 1956 in Mortgage Execution Case No.63 of 1944 and on 10th December 1952 in Mortgage Execution Case No.51 of 1952. The sales were subsequently confirmed. Possession was delivered to the Bank on 29th September 1952 and on 26th April 1953 of the other lands of the judgment debtor excepting the suit lands. Madhabi Lata Lala filed Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 2 of 1953 for setting aside the auction purchase by Mahaluxmi Bank Ltd. The case was dismissed. Madhabi Lata preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No.69 of 1953 which was allowed by the High Court Division on 24th August 1956, sale was set aside so far as Madhabi's interest was concerned on condition of her payment of Tk. 25,000/- to the Bank within six months from the date. As she fell in financial difficulties she sold the land and other lands to the appellant for Tk. 32,500/- by a registered sale deed, Ext. 3 dated 29th September 1958. Madhabi Latalala deposited Tk. 25.000/- in the aforesaid Miscellaneous case No. 2 of 1953 on 22nd February 1957 and got it set aside. 

 3. On 15th December 1960 the C.S. map produced by the plaintiff was made Ext. No.1, and the other copy of the C.S. map, Ext. 2 which is the exact replica of Ext. No.1 was filed on 2nd July 1962. Appellant and his predecessors have been paying rent to the khas Mohal in respect of the suit plot but rent-receipts were being granted in the name of Sarada Kripa Lala as owner. Rent receipts commencing from 1946 to 1955 could not. however, be produced as no time was granted by the Court. Appellant could not also produce the will and probate or oral evidence for the same reason. After purchasing the suit plot on 29th September 1958 from Madhabi Lata Lala appellant went to take possession of the jote but was obstructed by the respondent who is adjacent jote owner. He therefore, filed the aforesaid title suit. 

 4. Defendant-respondent contested the suit. In the written statement he denied all the material allegations and asserted that neither Sarada Kripa Lala nor Mohaluxmi Bank Ltd. had any right, title and possession in the suit land, plaintiff- appellant is not the real plaintiff but a mere name lender for his son. That the R.S. Khatian showing possession of the land in the name of Sarada Kripa Lala was wrong, that the suit land appertained to original jote Nos. 88/88. created in the name of Aparna Charan Kanangoe in Settlement Case No. 284 of 190 Jr 1908, a major portion of the land was recorded in the name of Aparna Charan Kanangoe as jote No. 81 and the remaining portion wrongly recorded in the name of one Sarda Kripa Lala as Jote No. 86. After taking settlement of the land Aparna Charan Kanangoe prayed for demarcation, of the suit land to khas Mahal department which granted his prayer and that the suit is barred by limitation and also by adverse possession.
